biggestGap: The chamber's architecture never comes forward of the board — every pier, wall and arch sits at or behind the far rank, so the outer quarters and the entire bottom band of frame are empty black and NOTHING in the image is cropped by any frame edge. The board's far edge, both side edges and the near kerb are all fully visible with void around them, which makes the scene read as a lit model on a table rather than a floor you are standing over. Build the piers as near-field objects: colossal, hard against and slightly FORWARD of the near kerb, close enough to be cut off by both the top and the bottom of frame and to occupy the outer ~20% of frame width on both sides, so the board runs off the left and right edges behind them.
critiqueDetail: I called panel A as the film instantly and with high confidence, and I was right. Say plainly what improved this round, because two round-3 blockers are genuinely gone. The top-left geometry leak — the dead-straight faceted black polygon edge exposing a brighter coursed wall behind it — is no longer present anywhere in frame; I looked for it specifically. The far symmetric colonnade with a fat column parked on the vanishing point is also gone. gradientAnisotropy has come from 1.247 to 1.492 against a reference of 1.462, so the directional structure of the room is now essentially correct, which was a -0.215 miss last round and is now +0.030. fracDeepShadow moved the right way, 0.0706 to 0.0813 against 0.1061. Hue is tight at 220.7 vs 223.6. Determinism holds: three separate captures at t=3, including the two dedicated back-to-back ones, are byte-identical (md5 f64e1f7eee0c9fa66f15630a3334c5f8), and no file under src/chamber changed during the capture window (last edit 05:50:14, captures ran 05:52-06:06), so this is a clean pass and not a quiet window. But the headline diagnosis from round 3 has not moved; it has gone backwards. Coarse-band detail is 0.00829 against the film's 0.02014 — 41 percent of reference, DOWN from last round's 0.01139 (57 percent). That number is the near-field mass measured directly, and the build lost ground on it. Meanwhile the mid band is 0.03784 against 0.02098, 180 percent of reference, up from 155 percent. The film's detailByBand is almost perfectly flat across scales (0.02014 / 0.02098 / 0.02019); ours is a pronounced hump — starved of big shapes, glutted with small ones. detailTotal 0.02485 vs 0.02036 is close, which is exactly the trap: the total looks fine while the shape says the energy is in the wrong place. Concretely, this round added marble veining, faceted rubble and a lot more candle flames — all mid and fine band — while the architecture stayed distant. Looking at the frame: the left and right walls are now soft rounded vertical folds that curve inward and meet in an arch across the top. They read as draped theatre curtains or a cave apse, not as carved Gothic piers — no flat faces, no arrises, no mouldings catching a grazing highlight, and their value sits so close to the void that they contribute almost no silhouette. They also hug the far half of the room; the nearest one is roughly level with the front rank, and forward of that there is nothing at all. The bottom-left and bottom-right corners of the frame are pure empty black with a couple of unsupported candle flames floating in them, which is the identical failure I described in round 3. Second, where the room ends is now WRONG IN A NEW WAY. The far wall is a brightly lit rectangular panel of coursed blocks, clean and legible, sitting dead on the board's axis and reading as the brightest architectural element in the upper frame. It is a crisp readable back wall at a measurable distance — the room reads as maybe 15 m deep. In the film the far end is a dark, curved, unresolved mass barely brighter than the surrounding void; you cannot tell where it stops. Trading round 3's rim-lit colonnade for a rim-lit masonry panel does not fix the problem, it relocates it. histogramEntropy 6.517 vs 6.894 (-0.377, worse than round 3's -0.143) is that panel plus the empty corners: too much of the frame is either flat void or flat lit wall, and not enough is the film's continuously modulated stone. warmFraction has also drifted the wrong way, 0.1127 vs 0.1390 (round 3 was +0.0027, now -0.0263) — despite there being visibly MORE flames, they are small, evenly spaced and lighting nothing, because there is no near stone within a metre of them to catch their falloff. In the film every flame sits against a mass it illuminates; here they burn in vacuum. That is an architecture symptom, not a lighting one.

Masonry is crude coursed block with heavy mortar rather than smooth carved Gothic. Render is also nondeterministic (85% of pixels differ between identical captures).

Real wins: the top-left geometry leak is gone, the far colonnade with its on-axis column is gone, gradientAnisotropy is now 1.492 vs 1.462 (was a -0.215 miss), and determinism is a clean pass across three byte-identical captures. But near-field mass REGRESSED — coarse-band detail fell to 0.00829 vs reference 0.02014 (41%, down from 57%) while the mid band rose to 180% of reference, so this round bought veining, rubble facets and extra flames instead of architecture. No pier, wall or piece is cropped by any frame edge; the board's far edge, both side edges and the near kerb all sit inside a black margin, so it reads as a lit model on a table. The side walls are soft rounded folds that read as draped curtains rather than carved piers, and the far end is now a clean brightly lit coursed-block panel on axis where the film has a dark unresolved mass.
